text:
maria: Heads-up — scheduling a rolling maintenance window for the 'scanline' cohort (az19 + az20). Tue 02:00–05:00 UTC. Scope: NIC microcode + GPU driver hotfix. Plan is soft drains + graceful kv-cache reseed. Aim: keep hosted pool >=95% availability.

aj: What's the expected GPU capacity impact? any heavy tenants mapped to scanline?

maria: Estimated impact ~6% of total GPU capacity for ~45m per cohort while they drain. We'll run staggered cohorts (az19 first, az20 30m later). Backfill from burst-pool + preheated spare nodes.

kevin: How are we handling model fallbacks? want automatic routing to smaller quantized variants if latency spikes.

maria: Yes — smart-routing policy "maint-fallback" will divert to compatible variants in eu-west when local capacity drops below threshold. Fallback window = 10m before trigger.

sam: Observability checklist: streaming latency SLOs, per-route token cost, and kv-cache hit rate. I'll wire up a smoke test to run every 5m during the window.

maria: thanks. add log keys: `scanline:maint` so we can filter. Also enable delta tracing for prefix-cache ops.

zara: customer comms draft: "Planned short maintenance, possible ~1–2% degradation for high-p99 workloads; no API key rotation required." Do we need tenant-specific notices?

aj: Only if they have pinned dedicated capacity in az19/az20 — list attached below.

maria: quick list: TenantA (critical, dedicated az19), TenantC (bursty, multi-region). We'll do a targeted canary for TenantA off-hours and coordinate with SEs.

kevin: Canary plan: pick 2 non-prod nodes in az19, drain and reboot, monitor 10m. If KV miss rate > 8% or p99 latency > 200ms, abort and rollback.

sam: Smoke test script (short):
```bash
# fetch a 4k token generation to assert latency
python infra/tests/smoke_gen.py --model redwood-4x --tokens 4000 --region az19
```
I'll run in a loop during canary.

maria: kubectl snippet for soft drain we'll use (grace 600s):
```bash
kubectl drain node/scanline-node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600 --timeout=15m
```
We'll follow with `kubectl uncordon` after healthchecks.

oncall-bot: Preflight checks: capacity-reserve >= 10%? false. Please confirm reserve bumped or backfill capacity validated.

maria: Confirmed — preheated burst nodes are online, reserve bumped to 12% for the window. Verified by autoscaler metrics.

azara: Ops note: cost estimate for backfill ~ $3.9k for the 3h window (spot + burst buffer). Flagging to finance.

aj: Any region-network constraints? az19 shares egress path with az18, previous window showed transient BGP flaps. We should stagger neighbor cohort by 1h to avoid correlated pressure.

maria: Good catch. We'll shift az20 start by +1h to reduce overlap with az18 planned work. New window: az19 02:00–03:15, az20 03:30–04:45 UTC.

kevin: Post-mortem ask: capture kernel and nvlink driver versions pre/post so we can validate perf regression.

maria: Will snapshot `/var/log/dmesg` and `nvidia-smi -q` output into artifacts path `s3://redwood-ops/maint/6570012345/`.

sam: Adding alerts: kv-cache-miss >= 5% sustained for 3m, p99 > 250ms for 5m, and error-rate > 0.5% should auto-trigger rollback.

oncall-bot: Rollback play: automatic fallback to previous driver if telemetry breach during canary + ops page ping.

zara: I'll schedule a short message to #support + emailed notice to TenantA SEs with the time changes.

maria: Final checklist: canary start 02:10 UTC (2 nodes), hold 20m, then proceed cohort drain. Run smoke tests every 5m, ops on-call monitor @aj and @kevin. If all green, full cohort sweep.

aj: :thumbsup: I'll be monitoring and have escalation ready.

kevin: one more: ensure dedicated KMS keys not touched by node reboots (we've seen HSM rekey delays). ops-runbook updated.

maria: noted. thanks everyone — will post final runbook and link to the runbook in here 30m before start.

maria: deploy-bot: scheduled maintenance window created -> id=maint-6570012345, owner=maria, cohorts=[az19,az20], backfill_pool=burst-02
